title: Electrical Circuits
seo_title: Primary 5 Science: Electrical Circuits Worksheets – Series and Parallel (with Answers)
standard_code: Primary 5: Energy forms and uses (Electrical systems: circuits)
standard_text: Recognise that an electric current flows only in a closed circuit and identify the components of a circuit (batteries, bulbs, wires and switches). Investigate the effect of the number and arrangement of batteries and bulbs (in series and in parallel) on the brightness of bulbs, and show an understanding of the safe and wise use of electricity (summary of the MOE Primary Science Syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Primary 5 science worksheets for Singapore pupils on electrical circuits: closed circuits, switches, bulbs and batteries in series and parallel, brightness, and electrical safety. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Current flows only in a closed circuit.
key_sub: Series or parallel changes how bright the bulbs are.
body_html:
How to think about it

An electric current flows only in a closed circuit.

  • A circuit needs a source (battery), wires, and components such as bulbs; a switch opens or closes the circuit.
  • Bulbs in series are dimmer, and if one fuses, all go out.
  • Bulbs in parallel are each as bright as one bulb alone, and if one fuses, the others stay lit.
  • More batteries in series make bulbs brighter. Batteries in parallel give the same brightness but last longer.
Example

Three bulbs are in parallel. One fuses. How many stay lit?

Each bulb has its own path

The other two paths are still closed

Answer: 2 bulbs.

Example

A second battery is added in series. What happens to the bulb?

More batteries in series push more current

Answer: It becomes brighter.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a bulb can light with one wire. The circuit must be a closed loop.
  • Thinking bulbs in parallel are dimmer than one bulb. Each is as bright as one bulb alone.
  • Thinking all bulbs go out when one bulb in parallel fuses.
  • Thinking an open switch lets current flow.

faq.q: What is the difference between series and parallel circuits?
faq.a: In series, the components are on one path, so if one bulb fuses all go out. In parallel, each bulb has its own path, so the others stay lit.

faq.q: Are bulbs in parallel brighter than bulbs in series?
faq.a: Yes. Each bulb in parallel is as bright as one bulb alone, while bulbs in series share the electrical energy and are dimmer.

faq.q: Why are home lights connected in parallel?
faq.a: So that each light can be switched on and off separately, and one fused bulb does not turn off the others.

items.q: What does a switch do?
c: turns a circuit on or off by closing or opening a gap
items.e: On or off.

items.q: Why should we never poke a metal object into a power socket?
c: Metal conducts electricity and can give a deadly electric shock.
It is safe if the object is small.
items.e: Mains electricity is very dangerous.

items.q: Why is it good to save electricity?
c: Most electricity in Singapore is made by burning natural gas, so saving it saves money and reduces pollution.
Electricity never runs out, so it does not matter.
items.e: Power stations burn fuels to make electricity.

items.q: A toy car motor changes electrical energy mainly into which form of energy?
items.e: A toy car motor gives out kinetic energy.

items.q: Why do batteries eventually stop working?
c: The chemicals inside get used up.
items.e: Some can be recharged.

items.q: Why is a smoke alarm usually battery-powered?
c: It keeps working even if the mains power goes off.

items.e: Reliability.

items.q: Which of these saves electricity?

drying clothes in the sun instead of a dryer
opening the fridge door for a long time
leaving the television on in an empty room
items.e: Saving electricity saves money and reduces the burning of fuels in power stations.

items.q: A bulb does not light even though the circuit looks complete. What should you check first?

items.q: Does a hairdryer usually run on mains electricity or on batteries?

items.q: Why should frayed electrical wires be replaced?

items.e: The plastic covering is an insulator for safety.

items.q: Why should used batteries be recycled and not put in the bin?

items.e: Recycle safely.

items.q: What should you do if you see a damaged electrical cable?

items.e: Safety first.

items.q: What is a circuit?
c: a complete loop that electricity can flow around
items.e: No gaps.

items.q: Why should you never touch a switch or plug with wet hands?
c: Water conducts electricity and could give you a shock.
items.e: Keep water away.

items.q: Which of these is safe to use in a school circuit?

items.q: Why does a torch need a switch?

items.q: Why do many devices use rechargeable batteries?

items.q: Why should we not overload a power socket with many plugs?

items.q: Which of these saves electricity?

items.e: Saving electricity saves money and reduces the burning of fuels in power stations.
